rationale:
Evidence. The raced baseline is iteration 7 (score 340.50): base_speed 1.5, kp 3.5, ki 0.05, kd 0.8, 12 mm sensors at y=0.06 (x = +/-0.04, +/-0.02, 0), last_direction. Oval finished 14 of 20 (finish rate 0.70, progress 0.973). S-bend progress was 0.424 and slalom progress 0.181, both ending off track. Iteration 6 to 7 was a clean single-factor step in kd (0.4 to 0.8), and it produced the largest gain in the record.

What I kept, changed and rejected after the round-2 critique:
(1) Kept kd 1.1, the 37 percent step from the raced kd 0.8, with every other value equal to iteration 7. The critique is right that kd response is nonlinear and that 1.1 is an extrapolation. I keep the step because it is the smallest change that can show whether the damping peak lies above 0.8. A larger step (1.4 or more) would confound the result if the peak is near 0.8.
(2) Accepted that the oscillation expectation was too vague. The per-track baselines at kd 0.8 are oval 0.328, s-bend 0.231 and slalom 0.207. The revert rule is now relative to each track's own value, not to the absolute 0.40 figure. Revert kd to 0.8 if steering_oscillation rises more than 25 percent on any track (oval above about 0.41, s-bend above about 0.29, slalom above about 0.26), or if oval finish falls below 0.6.
(3) Accepted that the slalom claim was inaccurate. Slalom was flat at 0.105 from iterations 0 to 6 and moved only at kd 0.8 (to 0.181). kd is therefore the first lever to move slalom, and I now expect kd 1.1 to matter on slalom as well as the s-bend. I do not predict a specific slalom value.
(4) Accepted that the decision rules were not complete. The keep rule now requires both conditions: oval finish at least 0.6 and at least one of s-bend or slalom progress rising above its iteration 7 value (0.424 or 0.181). If oval finish is between 0.6 and 0.7, the result is judged on the combined per-track evidence, since 20 trials give a standard error of about 0.10 on the finish rate.
(5) Partly accepted the seed-noise point. Oval finish is decided on 20 trials, so changes under about 0.1 in finish rate are not separable from noise. Progress on the s-bend and slalom is judged in pairs of seeds, because the disturbance is fixed per seed and track.
(6) Rejected base_speed 1.2. Completion (500 points) is within reach at 1.5 because oval finishes 70 percent of trials, so lowering speed would give up the largest term for an unsupported speed effect.
(7) Stated openly: this change does not address the start or first bend, which the earlier data point to as the early-failure location. A kd gain would not show that the robot can finish every track.

Expected result: oval finish rate holds at or above 0.7, s-bend progress rises above 0.424, slalom progress rises above 0.181, and steering_oscillation stays within the relative limits above. A three-track mean change under about 5 points should be treated as noise.

Decision rules for the next revision: (a) keep kd 1.1 if oval finish is at least 0.6 and at least one of s-bend or slalom progress rises, with oscillation within limits. (b) Revert to kd 0.8 if oval finish falls below 0.6 or oscillation exceeds its per-track limit. (c) If progress rises on all three tracks with oscillation flat, test kd 1.4 alone. (d) If progress is unchanged on all tracks, the next single test is base_speed alone (1.5 to 1.7).
